parsed.n_justification: The Naches River basin spans a strong west-to-east elevation, precipitation, and vegetation gradient (subalpine forest to shrub-steppe). 20 single columns sample this gradient with ~4 replicate clusters across 5 elevation/vegetation bands to resolve how ET partitioning varies with climate forcing and soil texture while keeping the ensemble computationally tractable.
assumptions: Study uses satellite-phenology (SP) or fully-prognostic BGC mode with default PFTs assigned from surface dataset for each Naches location
GSWP3/CRUNCEP atmospheric forcing (2000-2020) is used with an initial spin-up prior to the 21-year analysis run
Monthly and daily history output is sufficient; sub-daily h1 stream can be enabled if diurnal partitioning is required
Columns are run independently with no lateral hydrologic coupling; PFLOTRAN coupling reserved for subsurface partitioning follow-up
